title: Introduction to R
text:
Variables and Data Types

Numeric — numbers such as 3.14, 42
Integer — whole numbers with L suffix, e.g. 5L
Character — text values like "data"
Logical — TRUE or FALSE
Factor — categorical values with levels
Complex — numbers with imaginary parts like 1 + 2i



Show the code
x <- 5          # numeric
name <- "Alice" # character
flag <- TRUE    # logical
colors <- factor(c("red", "blue", "green"))



Variables store values in memory and can be reused later
R is dynamically typed: type depends on the stored value

title: Introduction to R
text:
Vectors and Sequences

Create ordered collections with c() and sequences with seq()
Useful for numeric data, indexes, and repeated values



Show the code
ages <- c(23, 35, 28)
seq(1, 100, 3)
seq(1, 2, length.out = 10)

title: Introduction to R
text:
Factors and Categorical Variables

Store categories or groups with fixed levels
Important for statistical modeling and reporting
Use factor() to make discrete labels or ordered categories



Show the code
gender <- factor(c("Male", "Female", "Male", "Female"),
                 levels = c("Male", "Female"))
physical_activity <- factor(sample(c(1, 2), 10, replace = TRUE),
                            levels = c(1, 2),
                            labels = c("Yes", "No"))

title: Introduction to R
text:
Lists and Matrices


Lists

Store mixed types in one object
Can contain vectors, data frames, functions, or other lists
Good for nested results and complex outputs



Show the code
my_list <- list(name = "Alice", score = 95, data = c(1, 2, 3))



Matrices

Two-dimensional arrays with a single data type
Ideal for numeric calculations, matrices, and linear algebra
Built from vectors using matrix(), cbind(), or rbind()



Show the code
m <- matrix(1:9, nrow = 3)

title: Introduction to R
text:
Data Structures

Data frames are the most common table structure in R
They combine columns of equal length and can contain different types
Lists and matrices are also important foundational structures



Show the code
my_data <- data.frame(
  ID = 1:5,
  Name = c("Alice", "Bob", "Charlie", "David", "Eva"),
  Age = sample(20:50, 5, replace = TRUE)
)

Installation

Install a single package:



Show the code

Install several packages:



Show the code
install.packages(c("tidyverse", "ggplot2", "readxl"))



Use pacman to install and load packages automatically:



Show the code
if (!require("pacman")) install.packages("pacman")
pacman::p_load(tidyverse, ggplot2, readxl, gtsummary, ggstatsplot, flextable)



pacman::p_load() installs missing packages and loads them in one command.

Setup Data

library(tidyverse)

clinic_wide <- tibble(
  id = 1:6,
  sex = c("Female", "Male", "Female", "Male", "Female", "Male"),
  age = c(22, 34, 29, 41, 37, 26),
  bmi = c(19.8, 27.2, 31.1, 24.3, 29.4, 22.6),
  fbs_0 = c(88, 110, 132, 96, 124, 91),
  fbs_3 = c(86, 104, 120, 94, 118, 89),
  ppbs_0 = c(126, 168, 214, 142, 176, 130),
  smoker = c("No", "Yes", "No", "Yes", "No", "No")
)

clinic_long <- tibble(
  id = c(1,1,2,2,3,3,4,4),
  visit = c("baseline", "3m", "baseline", "3m", "baseline", "3m", "baseline", "3m"),
  fbs = c(88, 86, 110, 104, 132, 120, 96, 94)
)

treatment_map <- tibble(
  id = 1:6,
  treatment = c("Diet", "Metformin", "Insulin", "Diet", "Metformin", "Diet")
)

title: Practical Application
text:
Case Study 1: Publication Figure
Scenario: Need publication-ready figure for medical journal
Requirements: - High resolution (300 DPI) - Grayscale-friendly - Clear statistical annotations - Professional formatting

title: Practical Application
text:
Publication Figure - Code


Code
# Treatment effect with confidence intervals
model <- lm(SysBP_12m ~ TreatmentGroup + Age + BMI_0m + SysBP_0m,
           data = health_data)

library(ggeffects)
effects <- ggpredict(model, terms = "TreatmentGroup")

p <- plot(effects) +
  labs(title = "Treatment Effect on Systolic Blood Pressure",
       subtitle = "Adjusted for age, BMI, and baseline BP",
       x = "Treatment Group",
       y = "Predicted Systolic BP (mmHg)",
       caption = "Error bars: 95% confidence intervals. n=500 per group.") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "none"
  )

# Save high-res
ggsave("figure1.tiff", p, width = 7, height = 5, dpi = 300)
ggsave("figure1.eps", p, width = 7, height = 5, device = cairo_ps)
